references.text: Joseph is taken to Egypt and sold to Potiphar, an Egyptian court official – the direct continuation of the Ishmaelites bringing him there.
Joseph reveals himself to his brothers and says that they sold him into Egypt, but that God sent him ahead to preserve life.
The psalmist mentions that Joseph was sold as a slave – a poetic summary of the sale described here.
The prophet Zechariah mentions thirty silver pieces as the price, a typological parallel to the price for which Joseph was sold.
Judas betrays Jesus for thirty pieces of silver, a typological parallel to Joseph being sold by his brothers for twenty silver pieces.
Stephen recounts that the patriarchs sold Joseph into Egypt out of jealousy, but that God was with him.
Direct reference back to the event that forms the basis for reconciliation and forgiveness.
